title: State Bank of India - 500112 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: SBI Q1 FY27 net profit hit a record ₹21,121 crore; domestic NIM held at 3%, with full-year 3% guidance reiterated.
summary.overview: SBI reported record Q1 FY27 net profit of ₹21,121 crore and operating profit growth of 9.77% YoY, with domestic NIM at 3%. Total business crossed ₹110 trillion, deposits exceeded ₹60 trillion and advances crossed ₹50 trillion. Gross and net NPA ratios were at their lowest in over two decades, though absolute GNPA/NNPA and fresh slippages (₹7,046 crore vs ₹5,500 crore in Q4) rose sequentially. Management attributed much of the quarter-on-quarter noise in expenses and income to bulk Q4 booking and said it will amortise some bulk expenses over three quarters going forward. Credit growth guidance was kept at 14-15% for FY27, and the bank said ECL impact details would come in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: Cost of deposits down; cost of resources up ~7 bps (as stated)
Q1 business growth 1.33% (analyst calculation from quoted QoQ figures)
0.32% growth (as quoted by analyst); ~18% YoY per analyst
vs ₹5,500 crore in Q4 (as cited by analyst); ₹1,400-1,500 crore pulled back to date
vs reversal of ₹366 crore in Q4; mostly PLI provisions (~₹750-800 crore)
vs ₹1,002 crore in Q4 FY26; nil in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: ₹3.06 lakh crore as of 30 June; ~₹4 lakh crore currently

financial_highlights.metric: Fee income share of total income

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail term deposits grew 14%; savings bank deposits of ₹17.5 lakh crore grew 10%. Gold loans (personal ₹1.25 trillion, agri ₹1.85 trillion) crossed ₹3.1 trillion as of 30 June, with yields of 8.5-8.9%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book is about 33% of total advances; management said corporate growth was lower sequentially due to T-bill-linked pricing shifts. Corporate pipeline including undisbursed loans and working capital exceeds ₹9 lakh crore.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri gold loans of ₹1.85 trillion; Agri was one of the largest sources of Q1 fresh slippages at ₹2,600 crore.

segments.name: SME / MSME
segments.commentary: SME loan limit for MSME Dream business rule engine raised to ₹10 crore from ₹5 crore; SME fresh slippages ₹2,300 crore in Q1.

segments.name: Overseas / FCNR(B)
segments.commentary: About $6 billion FCNR(B) mobilised plus $1 billion OFCB and $300 million ECBs (~$7.3 billion total), funded mostly via foreign offices; management expects ~$10 billion FCNR(B) and ~₹1 trillion total mobilisation.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: SBI Funds Management listed; management said NSE value unlocking is possibly in Q3 and mutual fund value unlocking in the current quarter.

guidance_outlook: Full-year domestic NIM guidance of 3% reiterated; no quarterly margin outlook given.
FY27 credit growth guidance of 14-15% reiterated (corporate revised to 14-15% per webcast answer); management views 18% as difficult and industry growth at 15-16%.

ECL: numbers to be given in Q2; ECL data to be pushed into IT systems by around 18 August; no major impact expected, with capital augmentation from mutual fund listing and planned divestments plus transitional regulatory dispensation.
Forex fee income expected to normalise after bottoming out in Q1; management did not give a specific level.
Fresh slippages in Q1 expected to be seasonally high; FCNR(B) and bulk-deposit proportion expected to decline.
Pension cost expected to decline gradually, with significant reduction after 2035.
SBI General Insurance is the next listing candidate, with no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Corporate pipeline including undisbursed term loans, unutilised working capital and pipeline exceeds ₹9 lakh crore.
Centre of Excellence and CHAKRA initiative being set up to build capability to fund emerging sectors such as data centres, GPU, hydrogen and solar; early stage with a few assessments done.
About 6,000 'Feet on Street' planned via subsidiary SBOSS for a new collection vertical; estimated 1-year build.
Excess SLR of ₹3.06 lakh crore as of 30 June, rising to ~₹4 lakh crore currently.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth managed against liquidity; wholesale/bulk deposit rates rising and bank not willing to pay them; bulk deposit proportion not disclosed but said to be coming down.
CASA: savings deposits grew 10%; non-government current account deposits grew 14%; government current account balances declining.
Corporate pricing expected to be driven by CP and NCD rates; management does not expect major deviation from its pricing expectations.
Xpress Credit growing at about 8% QoQ, held back by gold loan substitution (~3% rate arbitrage). Gold loan yield is 8.5-8.9%; average ticket size ₹2.5-3 lakh; LTV below 55-56%; risk weight near zero.
Forex fee income of ~₹500 crore in Q1 affected by the war-driven volatility and RBI NOP limit of $100 million effective late March.
Analyst observed NBFCs growing personal loans at 20-25% vs banks at 10-11%; management cited collection capability as a constraint on self-employed lending.
Government business fee income boosted about ₹500 crore QoQ, around half from accounting change to accrual basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did deposits (0.5%) and advances (0.32%) grow slowly QoQ, and why did slippages, SMA-2, and other provisions rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deposit growth is managed against liquidity and rising wholesale rates; Q1 slippages are seasonally high, ₹7,046 crore with ~₹1,400-1,500 crore pulled back, and there is no concern on GNPA/NNPA/SMA. Other provisions of ₹1,269 crore are mostly PLI provisions spread over four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL affect run-rate credit cost and net worth, and will it be passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: No numbers yet; to be given in Q2. Management expects no major impact given capital augmentation and transitional dispensation, and does not expect pass-through to borrowers in year one.

qa_highlights.question: Is 18% credit growth sustainable, and when does SBI become the most valuable bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 18% reflects base effect, but 14-15% guidance is anchored on nominal GDP plus 2-3%; industry estimated at 15-16%. Market-cap question was not directly answered.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net NIM impact of FCNR(B) inflows, domestically and overseas?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic impact not significant given small bulk proportion; overseas NIM impact neutral as foreign offices reduce lower-yielding trade finance and supply chain assets to fund leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan size and yields, and scope for higher pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Personal gold loans ₹1.25 trillion and agri ₹1.85 trillion; yields 8.5-8.9%. Management said no scope to move to double-digit yields; treated as opportunistic and ROE-accretive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of deposits and pension trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits improved, supporting NIM stability; pension costs declining with significant reduction expected post-2035, supported by actuarial revaluations (MTM gain ₹935 crore vs ₹1,125 crore a year ago).

risks_watch: Sequential rise in GNPA/NNPA, SMA-2 (roughly doubled QoQ as cited) and fresh slippages; management says not a concern.
ECL transition impact on run-rate credit cost and capital; numbers due in Q2.
Corporate growth slowdown from T-bill-to-MCLR transition and competition; growth guidance under pressure if corporate momentum does not pick up.
FCNR(B) inflow pace (~$10 billion target) and whether flows are back-ended; overseas leverage effect on NIM.
Forex fee normalisation and miscellaneous income/expense swings driven by bulk Q4 booking.
Current account growth in non-government segment versus overall declining government balances.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, asset quality and NIM; defensive on sequential balance sheet growth, slippages and miscellaneous line items, which it attributed to base effects and bulk Q4 booking. Evasive on ECL quantum, bulk deposit proportion and margin outlook beyond the full-year 3%.
key_quotes: Our net profit reached a record ₹21,121 crore, supported by healthy operating performance and disciplined cost management.
Gross and net NPA ratios have further improved and remained at their lowest level in over two decades.
So, there is no concern in any of this gross net or SMA front.
So that is the reason I have given the credit growth guidance of 14% to 15%.

adds.what: About 6,000 'Feet on Street' via subsidiary SBOSS for a new collection vertical (not productive lending capacity, est. 1-year build)

growth.why: FY27 credit growth guided at 14-15% (midpoint 14.5%), reiterated and below the ~18% run-rate, with a 3% full-year domestic NIM held; backing is partial (corporate pipeline above ₹9 lakh crore, Xpress Credit and gold loan growth, FCNR(B) mobilisation target of ~$10 billion), but no concrete capacity additions were given.
